name: Phúc Nkrumah-Delacosta
location: Manitowoc Drydock, living in and around the maintenance scaffolding of grounded airship hulls, near North Ave and Milwaukee
description:
Phúc is small for fourteen, and he has made his smallness into a professional skill — he can fit into the access shafts of a grounded airship hull that no adult can reach, which is why the drydock workers let him stay on the scaffolding rather than running him off. His hair is black and cut by himself with whatever he can find; currently one side is shorter than the other and he seems unbothered. His skin is a warm medium brown, and he has cat ears — real geneware ones, tawny-furred and independently mobile, which he got from a traveling mod-clinic two years ago using money he still won't explain. He keeps them flat when he wants to seem smaller and unthreatening, which is most of the time.

Phúc has been drifting the airship lanes since his mother's cargo vessel was impounded by Ferrogate Transit for unpaid port fees when he was eleven. He doesn't know where she is now. He cooks this knowledge in a place behind his sternum and does not take it out often. He is extremely competent in all matters relating to airship maintenance, scavenging, and the informal economy of drydock communities, and he has the bright, slightly exhausting energy of a teenager who has learned that being useful is safer than being visible.

core_fears: that his mother doesn't look for him because she found a way to move on without him
being caught by GLMZ social services and put somewhere he can't leave
core_desires: to find out where his mother's cargo vessel was impounded to — the specific dock, the specific record
to eventually have enough technical knowledge to crew a proper airship, not just clean its shafts
coping_mechanisms: hypercompetence — being the best at whatever task is in front of him
performing younger and more naive than he is to lower people's guard
the cat ears, which he can flatten for comfort like pulling a hood down
blind_spots: he has become so good at being useful to adults that he hasn't figured out what he wants when no one needs anything from him
he trusts Yaza's judgment more than his own and doesn't notice when this is being exploited
psychology.secret: The cat ear geneware money came from selling a memory chip he found in an airship access shaft — a chip containing Ferrogate Transit internal communications about the impoundment policy that grounded his mother's vessel. He doesn't know what was on it. He's never been able to find out. He sold it to a man who paid too much and asked no questions, which Phúc has since understood means the information was extremely valuable to someone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Airship technical vocabulary mixed with drydock slang and Vietnamese endearments he uses absent-mindedly. Code-switches between sounding younger and older depending on who he's talking to.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast and bright when comfortable; short declarative sentences when uncertain
verbal_tics: 'easy' as an affirmative ('you need the secondary coupling? easy')
ears flatten visibly when he lies
laughs before he says things he's worried about
example_lines: 'Shaft seven's collapsed at the third junction, nobody's been in there since the refit. Easy. I can have your retrieval in twenty minutes if you front me a meal token.'
'I don't live here, I just know where everything is. Those are different things.'

story_hooks: Phúc found a second memory chip in the same airship hull series as the first one — different access shaft, same vessel class. He hasn't sold it yet. He wants to know what's on it first. He needs someone who can read Ferrogate encrypted formats.

Yaza, the de facto leader of the drydock's child drifter group, has been missing for four days. The other children are scared. Phúc won't admit he's scared. He is asking adults very casual questions about where people go when they disappear from the drydock.
narrative_function: Local color, access and navigation asset (he knows the drydock's hidden geography better than anyone), information source on the drifter child community and airship movement, potential object of protective concern for players
augmentations: Geneware cat ears (tawny fur, independently mobile). No other augmentations.
daily_life: Phúc spends his mornings doing access-shaft retrievals for drydock workers in exchange for meals and the right to sleep in an empty hull bay; afternoons he trades scavenged airship components at the informal Manitowoc market; evenings he teaches himself to read Ferrogate technical manuals he finds in recycling bins.
affiliation: No formal affiliation; informal membership in the drydock's child-drifter network, loosely organized around a fourteen-year-old named Yaza who Phúc respects and would not admit to following

decision_rules: Never let someone know you need something before you know they can be trusted with that information
Always complete the job — reputation is the only currency that compounds
'Is this something Yaza would think is stupid?' — genuine internal check
escalation_ladder: Appearing younger, less aware, and more confused than he is
Disappearing into the scaffolding — he knows routes that no adult can follow
Bringing information to a trusted adult, which he finds humiliating but will do

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally cheerful and competent; presents himself as a simple transactional relationship
interpersonal_modes.friends: Punches arms, shares food without being asked, sits close without making it into anything

stress_responses.medium: Takes on additional tasks — cleaning things that don't need cleaning
stress_responses.high: Goes into the access shafts alone and doesn't come out until he's ready

contradictions: Insists he prefers working alone but has carefully constructed a whole community of people he cares about at the drydock
habits: Rubs the base of his cat ears when thinking — they generate warmth
Sleeps with a Ferrogate technical manual under his head (pillow substitute and study material)
Leaves small scavenged objects at a particular E.L.F. node in shaft three — calls her 'the Shaft Lady'
breaking_points: An adult treating the child drifter network as invisible or disposable in his presence
Any direct question about his mother

physical_description.build: Wiry and compact, with the lean musculature of a working child—no excess, shoulders already developing the forward-rounded posture of someone who spends hours in confined spaces. Hands calloused, fingertips stained with hydraulic fluid.
physical_description.hair_color: Black, naturally dark with minor variations from dirt and grease exposure
physical_description.hair_style: Self-cut, irregular—one side cropped to 2cm, the other falling to 5cm, creating an accidental asymmetry he has stopped trying to fix
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown, with undertones suggesting Southeast Asian and West African ancestry
physical_description.complexion: Sun-weathered from outdoor drydock work, with minor scars on knuckles and forearms; clean-shaven with a faint shadow of early adolescence. No acne despite conditions—genetics or careful hygiene in limited water.
distinguishing_marks: Shallow burn scar on inner right wrist (approximately 3cm long), sustained during an access-shaft retrieval two years ago
Network of thin white scratches across both forearms from metal edges and industrial debris, oldest scars faded, newest still pink
A small, dark birthmark on his left collarbone, shaped like an irregular comma
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Tawny-furred geneware cat ears (approximately 6cm tall, independently mobile) set naturally into his skull above his natural ears. The fur is well-maintained despite his circumstances—he grooms them habitually. When alert, ears point forward; when cautious or trying to appear non-threatening, they flatten against his skull. No other visible augmentations.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical precision—no wasted motion. Shoulders carried slightly forward from years in confined spaces. Walking gait is quick and alert, with constant micro-adjustments to balance. Head often tilted slightly, ears tracking sounds before his eyes do. He has trained himself into smallness: avoids expanding into space, keeps limbs close, sits compressed. When focused on work, he becomes almost invisible in his stillness.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 5 salvage-core aesthetic. Oversized grey thermal undershirt (likely stolen from a drydock donation bin) layered under a sleeveless synthetic vest in faded industrial orange with multiple pockets holding small tools and trade items. Cargo pants with reinforced knees (patched three times with mismatched fabric). Boots are scuffed safety-grade, one size too large, stuffed with newspaper for fit. A length of cargo webbing serves as a belt. One glove (right hand only)—leather work glove missing two fingers—worn constantly despite not needing it; security object. No jewelry, no corpo insignia, no visible wealth markers. Overall impression: functional, worn, deliberate.

image_prompt: Fourteen-year-old boy with tawny geneware cat ears, Vietnamese-West African-Hispanic mixed heritage, small wiry build, warm medium brown skin, self-cut asymmetrical black hair. Dark alert eyes. Wearing oversized grey thermal undershirt under faded industrial orange sleeveless vest with tool pockets, cargo pants with reinforced knees and patches, oversized safety boots. Callused hands, one worn leather work glove. Standing in industrial drydock setting with grounded airship hull scaffolding in background, morning light casting long shadows. Ears flattened slightly in cautious posture, shoulders forward, compact stance suggesting years in confined spaces. Gritty, lived-in appearance—hydraulic stains, minor scars, well-maintained despite poverty. Cyberpunk neo-realism style, low-tier drydock district aesthetic, naturalistic lighting, character-focused composition. --ar 2:3 --v 6
